root_idea.summary: The root centers on seeking refuge by turning to, attaching oneself to, or taking shelter with something protective.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of taking refuge extends to things that cling to, remain with, or shelter beneath something else.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I dictionary citation form.
Displayed as the distinct causative Form IV verb.
Displayed as the distinct Form X verb.
Displayed as the Quranic nominal and formula مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ.

senses.definition: To seek protection or refuge in someone or something; to have recourse to a protector and rely on that protection.
senses.usage_conditions: Commonly constructed with بِـ for the protector and with مِنْ or عَنْ for the danger or act avoided. Quranic usage includes seeking refuge in God and in other beings.

senses.definition: To place someone under protection; to seek or provide refuge for someone with a protector.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative construction, as in seeking protection for a person through another protector.

senses.definition: To seek protection or refuge by turning to a protector.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic command, the form directs the addressee to seek refuge in God, conventionally by saying أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ.

senses.definition: A formula of seeking refuge in God: “God forbid,” or “I seek refuge in God from that.”
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ, often before or in response to a clause describing an act being rejected or disclaimed; in Quranic usage it functions as an exclamatory refuge formula rather than the literal place-sense of “refuge.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a female animal: to remain with and attend her young, keeping close to it for protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form I usage described of a female that stays with her offspring while it is young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female that has recently given birth and is in the early period of remaining with her young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a female gazelle, she-camel, mare, or similar animal; authorities variously specify roughly seven to fifteen days after giving birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of flesh-meat: to cling or adhere to the bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized expression describing meat that remains attached to a bone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause or enable someone to seek protection; to invoke or provide protection for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction, commonly with بِـ naming the protector or means of protection; with God as subject, it can mean to grant protection or preserve someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To charm or fortify someone against evil, illness, envy, destruction, or trial by invoking God, divine names, recitation, or an amulet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional protective or apotropaic practice, including reciting the protective chapters or using a charm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek protection or refuge from one another, or to rely on one another’s protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal Form VI usage is specifically attested in the context of war.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree or other object beneath or within which one takes refuge or shelter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a physical refuge or sheltering object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone, tree-trunk, or similar object surrounded by material blown against it and around it by the wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for something around which wind-borne matter accumulates.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fallen leaves that shelter against or gather around a rising object such as a building, hill, or mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the leaves’ taking shelter against the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vile or ignoble people; the worse, worst, or vilest of mankind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective evaluative noun for persons of especially low status or character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Escape from someone without being beaten or killed, despite being frightened, beaten, or attacked with intent to kill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the idiom أَفْلَتَ فُلَانٌ مِنْهُ عَوَذًا, describing escape from a threatened or attempted assault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave someone only because of dislike or hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مَا تَرَكْتُهُ إِلَّا عَوَذًا مِنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An amulet, phylactery, or charm intended to protect its wearer from the evil eye, fright, or demonic harm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The item may bear an inscription, and the term is also used for a protective charm or recitation; its relation to Quranic inscriptions is part of the classical discussion, not a Quranic use of the QAC forms here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Birds taking refuge in a mountain or another sheltered place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or collective usage for birds that have saved themselves by taking shelter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage or plants growing beneath thorn-trees, trees, stones, or other rising objects that shelter or protect them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plants may be difficult or impossible for grazing animals to reach because of the rugged ground or protecting growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who seeks protection or preservation, especially by taking refuge in God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle may be used in a refuge formula or as an absolute complement expressing earnest seeking of protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of four northern stars forming a quadrilateral around a smaller star.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional astronomical designation for stars in the head of Draco.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A refuge or place to which one has recourse for protection; also a time of resort and an infinitive meaning seeking protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the broader literal noun and verbal-noun range; the Quranic expression مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ is presented separately under the Quranic nominal form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: مُعْوِذَاتٌ: she-camels that have their young with them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural participial usage associated with females accompanied by their offspring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place of a horse’s collar, or the feathered or curling part of its coat at that place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine anatomical term, apparently associated with the suspension of charms or amulets there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel said to remain continually in one place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reported and lexicographically disputed reading in the cited entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two protective Quran chapters, al-Falaq and the chapter following it, al-Nās.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained by their opening with قُلْ أَعُوذُ and, in another explanation, by their function of preserving from evil; المُعَوِّذَاتُ may additionally include the preceding chapter.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers refuge-seeking and the Quranic refuge formula.

Fallen leaves sheltering against a rising object.
Idiomatic escape without being killed or beaten.
Active participle for one seeking protection.
Broader refuge, place, time, and infinitive sense.
Added plural usage for she-camels with young.
Synonymic cross-reference to the amulet meaning.

cautions: The historical verse citation associated with the Form X discussion is not used as a modern word-level example; the examples here use independently supplied QAC locations.
The reported camel sense of مُعَوَّذٌ is retained as a Classical meaning but is marked as lexicographically disputed.
The Quranic مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ formula is kept separate from the broader Classical noun meaning “refuge” or “place of resort.”
